items.title: CVE-2026-42018: JFrog JFrog Artifactory Improper Authentication Vulnerability
items.one_liner: JFrog Artifactory has an authentication bypass bug actively tracked by CISA that leaks internal tokens even when anonymous access is disabled.
items.summary: CISA has listed CVE-2026-42018 in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, covering an improper authentication flaw in JFrog Artifactory. The bug allows an unauthenticated caller to receive an internal anonymous-user token even when anonymous access is explicitly disabled, potentially exposing sensitive repository assets. CISA has mandated that federal agencies apply vendor mitigations or discontinue using the software by September 25, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Audit JFrog Artifactory deployments and apply patches immediately to prevent unauthorized access to internal artifact tokens.

claims.text: JFrog Artifactory exposes internal anonymous-user tokens to unauthenticated callers when anonymous access is disabled.

items.title: CVE-2026-14873 (HIGH 8.0): The Bulk Password Reset plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to privilege escalation via account takeover in al…
items.one_liner: WordPress administrators must immediately patch or remove the Bulk Password Reset plugin to prevent subscriber-level privilege escalation.
items.summary: A privilege escalation vulnerability affects the Bulk Password Reset plugin for WordPress in all versions up to and including 1.3.3. The flaw stems from insufficient user identity validation prior to updating sensitive account details, allowing authenticated attackers with subscriber-level access or higher to alter arbitrary user email addresses. Attackers can leverage this capability to reset passwords and achieve full account takeover of vulnerable sites. The vulnerability carries a CVSS base score of 8.0.
key_facts: Affected product: Bulk Password Reset plugin for WordPress

items.summary: A critical eval injection vulnerability has been identified in Apache Camel K, tracked as CVE-2026-80351 with a CVSS score of 9.8. items.title: 7 questions for assessing Cyber Resilience Act codebase readiness
items.one_liner: The EU's Cyber Resilience Act mandatory vulnerability reporting takes effect, requiring immediate compliance for digital product manufacturers.
items.summary: Starting September 11, 2026, manufacturers selling products with digital elements in the European Union face mandatory reporting requirements under the Cyber Resilience Act. items.title: Crypto customers targeted by scammers after email marketing provider breach
items.one_liner: A SAML flaw at email provider Brevo allowed attackers to launch targeted crypto-phishing campaigns against newsletter subscribers.
items.summary: An attacker breached email marketing provider Brevo by exploiting a SAML SSO flaw on September 10, gaining access to 138 customer accounts. The threat actor used 6 compromised accounts to launch targeted phishing campaigns against cryptocurrency newsletter subscribers, while exporting contact lists from 43 accounts. Major hardware wallet and crypto service providers such as Trezor, CoinTracking, and BitBox were targeted; Trezor warned its roughly 347,000 subscribers about a fraudulent email regarding a nonexistent "STM32 Entropy Bug" designed to trick users into giving up wallet recovery phrases.
key_facts: Breach date: September 10, 2026 at 6:30 AM UTC
items.bottom_line: Cryptocurrency platforms and users must remain highly vigilant against third-party supply-chain phishing attacks designed to steal seed phrases.

items.title: MantaxOtax Android Malware Combines Ransomware With Spyware
items.one_liner: MantaxOtax is a dual-purpose Android threat that steals sensitive data while simultaneously locking devices to extort victims.
items.summary: The MantaxOtax Android malware is a sophisticated threat that combines ransomware-style file encryption with extensive spyware capabilities. Distributed via sideloading, the malware uses Android Accessibility services to gain broad control, intercepting credentials, messages, and OTPs while recording screen activity. It targets Indonesian users and employs a C2 infrastructure that resolves domains via GitHub to maintain persistence. The malware also features aggressive UI-based harassment, including repeating alerts and text-to-speech commands, to pressure victims.
key_facts: Capabilities: AES file encryption, credential theft, screen recording, OTP interception
Abuse: Android Accessibility API, MediaProjection API
items.bottom_line: Android users are at risk of total device compromise and data theft from this malware, which bypasses standard security by abusing Accessibility services.

items.title: Check Point Discloses Two 9.8-Rated VPN Certificate Flaws Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
items.one_liner: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in Check Point VPN infrastructure require immediate patching or mitigation to prevent unauthenticated exploitation.
items.summary: Check Point has patched two critical, 9.8-rated vulnerabilities in its firewall and management products that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution. CVE-2026-85102 stems from improper certificate trust validation during VPN negotiation, while CVE-2026-85103 is a heap-based buffer overflow triggered during ASN.1 certificate decoding. The flaws affect Quantum Security Gateways, Security Management Servers, and Spark firewalls. Check Point has begun an automatic rollout of fixes via Live Patch and released updated Jumbo Hotfixes for affected versions.

items.title: Gigabud Creates Android Work Profiles to Hide From Banking App Malware Checks
items.one_liner: The Gigabud banking trojan uses Android work profiles via a helper app to hide malicious apps from security scans.
items.summary: The Gigabud Android banking trojan now installs a secondary helper app named Vwork that establishes an isolated Android work profile on infected devices. By cloning a tampered banking app inside this work profile, the malware effectively hides from security checks executed by genuine banking applications running in the device's main profile, preventing fraud alerts. Gigabud arrives via sideloaded apps masquerading as government portals or national airlines, subsequently requesting Accessibility permissions to take remote control of the device and execute fraudulent transactions via screen overlays. Security firm Group-IB confirmed active exploitation of this technique on devices in Indonesia.
items.bottom_line: Mobile banking malware can bypass client-side security checks by isolating fraudulent apps inside enterprise Android work profiles.

items.title: Cisco FMC Flaws Exploited to Steal Credentials and Deploy Qilin Ransomware
items.one_liner: State-sponsored actors and Qilin ransomware operators are actively exploiting critical Cisco Secure FMC authentication bypass flaws.
items.summary: Cisco revealed that three threat clusters linked to state-sponsored and ransomware operations are actively exploiting two recently patched vulnerabilities in Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) software. The critical vulnerability CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0), an authentication bypass in the web interface, is being leveraged by actors like UAT-12197 and UAT-11823 to execute script files, deploy web shells, and harvest credentials. Simultaneously, CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3) is being exploited by the UAT-11988 ransomware group for initial access to conduct living-off-the-land reconnaissance and deploy Qilin ransomware. CISA added CVE-2026-20079 to its KEV catalog and mandated federal agencies to apply patches.
items.bottom_line: Unpatched Cisco Secure FMC appliances are actively targeted in the wild for root compromise and ransomware deployment, requiring immediate hotfix deployment.

items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
items.one_liner: Chinese threat actors leveraged an active Chrome zero-day and Windows kernel escape exploiting a temporary patch gap.
items.summary: Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo exploited a multi-stage zero-day exploit chain in Google Chrome and Windows against NGOs in September 2026. The chain leveraged a reflected XSS on a US university website to redirect victims to a Google Chrome type-confusion zero-day in the V8 engine (CVE-2026-85046), combined with a WebAssembly defect (CVE-2026-87491) to escape the V8 sandbox and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to break out of the browser sandbox. Although CVE-2026-85046 had been fixed upstream in the Chromium codebase on August 4, 2026, a patch gap existed because no stable release of Google Chrome had incorporated the fix at the time of the attacks. Volexity discovered the activity and identified distinct post-exploitation payloads deployed by each actor.
key_facts: CVE-2026-85046: Chrome V8 type confusion zero-day
CVE-2026-85880: Windows kernel privilege escalation / sandbox escape
items.bottom_line: Upstream code fixes do not protect users until a stable browser build is released, exposing a critical patch gap exploited by APT groups.

items.title: CVE-2026-84939 (CRITICAL 9.1): Path traversal vulnerability in Apache FreeMarker template loading mechanism, if the attacker can specify an…
items.one_liner: A critical path traversal vulnerability in Apache FreeMarker allows unauthorized file access via malformed locale identifiers.
items.summary: A critical path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-84939, CVSS 9.1) has been identified in the Apache FreeMarker template loading mechanism. The flaw occurs when an attacker can specify an arbitrary malformed locale identifier and the default localized lookup configuration setting is enabled. Affected versions span from 2.2.0 through 2.3.34, and users are urged to upgrade to version 2.3.35 or disable localized lookup. While file access remains restricted by the configured TemplateLoader, certain loaders could potentially expose files beyond their intended base directories.
items.bottom_line: Organizations using Apache FreeMarker versions 2.2.0 through 2.3.34 must upgrade to 2.3.35 or disable localized lookup to prevent exploitation.

items.title: CVE-2026-82441: Apache Storm Nimbus: Cross-Tenant Blob Deletion and Cluster Denial of Service via Unvalidated Topology Dependency Keys
items.one_liner: A critical vulnerability in Apache Storm allows unauthenticated users to delete arbitrary blobs and crash the entire cluster via malformed topology submissions.
items.summary: Apache Storm Nimbus versions 3.0.0 before 3.1.0 are vulnerable to cross-tenant blob deletion and cluster-wide denial of service due to unvalidated topology dependency keys. A malicious user can submit a topology referencing another user's blob keys, causing those blobs to be deleted during cleanup. Furthermore, if a dependency key is missing, the Nimbus service will enter an infinite loop of acquiring and surrendering leadership, effectively disabling the cluster. Users are advised to upgrade to 3.1.0 or restrict topology submission to trusted principals.
key_facts: Vulnerability: Cross-tenant blob deletion and DoS
items.bottom_line: Upgrade to Apache Storm 3.1.0 immediately to prevent cluster-wide denial of service and cross-tenant data loss.

items.title: The AI Supply Chain Has a Security Problem, and Much of It Is Sitting on the Open Internet
items.one_liner: Tens of thousands of self-hosted AI endpoints and model servers are exposed to the public internet without authentication, risking resource abuse.
items.summary: A study by Mysterium VPN reveals that tens of thousands of self-hosted AI endpoints—including model servers, agent-building platforms, and vector stores—are publicly exposed to the internet without authentication. Scanning index data identified 36,769 reachable endpoints across tools like Open WebUI, vLLM, LocalAI, and llama.cpp, with only 2.02% returning an HTTP authentication challenge. Specifically, Open WebUI accounted for 18,529 reachable instances with almost none gated, while Ollama featured thousands of instances returning identifying strings and HTTP 200 responses. This exposure enables unauthorized third parties to hijack hardware resources for text generation, creating significant resource-abuse risks known as LLMjacking.
items.bottom_line: Exposing self-hosted AI model servers and chat interfaces to the public internet without authentication exposes local hardware to resource theft and LLMjacking.

items.title: CVE-2026-82438: Apache Storm Webapp: Authenticated API Responses Exposed to Arbitrary Web Origins
items.one_liner: Apache Storm Webapp 3.0.0-3.1.0 flaws allow unauthorized origin access to authenticated cluster data.
items.summary: Apache Storm Webapp versions 3.0.0 before 3.1.0 contain three separate vulnerabilities allowing unrelated origins to read authenticated API responses via exposed CORS credentials, reflected origin headers, and forced JSONP callbacks. Users are advised to upgrade to version 3.1.0 or place endpoints behind a reverse proxy that strips sensitive headers and callback parameters.
items.bottom_line: Apache Storm Webapp versions before 3.1.0 allow arbitrary web origins to steal authenticated API responses, requiring an immediate upgrade or reverse-proxy mitigation.

items.title: CVE-2026-82435: Apache Storm Worker: Unauthenticated Remote Memory Exhaustion in the Worker Messaging Decoder
items.one_liner: Apache Storm workers can be crashed by unauthenticated attackers sending frames that trigger excessive memory allocation before authentication occurs.
items.summary: Apache Storm Worker versions 3.0.0 before 3.1.0 are vulnerable to unauthenticated remote memory exhaustion. The Netty message decoder processes frames before SASL authentication is enforced, allowing an unauthenticated peer to trigger large memory allocations by sending a single frame with a large length field. This can lead to worker instability or crashes. Users are advised to upgrade to 3.1.0 or restrict network access to worker ports.
items.bottom_line: Upgrade to Apache Storm 3.1.0 to ensure message decoding only occurs after successful authentication.

items.title: India’s SEBI Seeks Major Changes to Unpopular Auction System
items.one_liner: SEBI proposed major structural changes to India's new closing auction system to address extreme market volatility during derivatives expiry.
items.summary: India's Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed major revisions to the closing auction system (CAS) introduced a month ago, following severe volatility, index rebalancing swings, and criticisms from traders and proprietary firms. The proposed changes include shortening the auction window from 20 minutes to 10 minutes, shifting the start time from 3:15 p.m. to 3:30 p.m., and cutting post-auction derivatives trading to five minutes. Additionally, SEBI put forward two options for calculating derivatives expiry settlement prices: a blended volume-weighted average price (VWAP) combining the final 30 minutes of continuous trading with the 10-minute auction, or returning entirely to the previous continuous-trading VWAP method. Public comments are open until October 3.
key_facts: Regulator: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
items.bottom_line: SEBI's proposed overhaul of the month-old closing auction system gives market participants alternative derivatives settlement methods to curb expiry-day volatility.

Additional proposals include shifting auction timings to follow regular market close at 3:30 p.m., stopping the dissemination of indicative index values during CAS to prevent confusion, cutting post-CAS derivatives trading windows, and restricting the cancellation of limit orders placed beyond 1% from the reference price. Public comments on the consultation paper are open until October 3.

items.one_liner: Researchers are using ChatGPT, Codex, and custom deep-learning models to scan genomic databases and accelerate the discovery of new antibiotics.
items.summary: Bioengineer César de la Fuente and his lab are using artificial intelligence to tackle antimicrobial resistance by searching the genetic codes of living and extinct organisms for new antimicrobial molecules. items.title: GuardBreaker: Derailing AI-assisted malware analysis with a code comment
items.one_liner: The GuardBreaker technique uses decoy prompts in code comments to trip LLM safety filters and halt malware analysis.
items.summary: ESET researchers discovered a novel adversarial evasion technique named GuardBreaker, used by the Russia-aligned group UAC-0099 against a target in Ukraine. The technique involves inserting a decoy request for instructions on building a nuclear weapon into a VBScript comment to trigger safety guardrails in LLM-powered code scanners, causing them to halt inspection before reaching the malicious payload. This simple prompt injection exploits architectural flaws in LLMs that fail to separate untrusted content from trusted instructions. Similar supply-chain attacks have involved fabricated system instructions, context-window exhaustion techniques, and direct commands to classify malicious packages as clean.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can bypass LLM-powered code scanners by embedding adversarial prompt injection payloads directly into code comments.

items.title: The context tax: why your coding agent reads the same 600 lines 400 times
items.one_liner: Semantic code graphs eliminate the 'context tax' where coding agents waste millions of tokens on repeated grep and file reads.
items.summary: Coding agents operating in large codebases often waste millions of context tokens by repeatedly using grep, file reads, and wide slices because they lack internal code navigation maps. Sonar Research illustrates this 'context tax' using a pull request in their SemSitter engine where an agent repeatedly grepped and read files to resolve a method's definition. To solve this inefficiency, their SemSitter semantic navigation engine maintains a Unified Dependency Graph, allowing agents to query nodes and typed relationships directly instead of relying on brute-force file reads.
key_facts: Token consumption example: 156 million context tokens and peak 459k window on an 800-line PR
items.bottom_line: Providing coding agents with structural dependency graphs instead of raw file reads dramatically reduces context window bloat and token waste.

items.one_liner: Shift vulnerability management from isolated severity scores to continuous autonomous attack path validation.
items.summary: Security teams are encouraged to move beyond static vulnerability severity scores and prioritize autonomous penetration testing to evaluate actual attack paths. While critical vulnerabilities look alarming, they may pose minimal risk if isolated by strong segmentation and access controls, whereas chained medium-severity flaws can lead directly to critical assets. Microsoft patched the issue on June 10, 2026, by introducing a readers-writer lock (AcquireSRWLockShared) and a shutdown flag to prevent concurrent access during teardown. A proof-of-concept mock lab has been released to demonstrate the double-fetch/TOCTOU bug class, though it does not target the live service.

items.title: OpenClaw went viral. Meet the maintainers building and securing it.
items.one_liner: OpenClaw maintainers discuss managing thousands of AI-generated pull requests, contributor trust, and securing a viral open source project.
items.summary: OpenClaw creator Peter Steinberger and project maintainers discuss the rapid growth and security challenges of the personal AI assistant project in a video interview. Started in November 2025, the repository expanded to roughly 388,000 stars, 81,000 forks, and over 80,000 commits by August 2026. The maintainers highlight how automated contributor tools flooded the project with hundreds of simulated pull requests, shifting the core challenge from attracting participation to filtering high-volume noise. They also share strategies for welcoming non-developer contributors who utilize AI agents, balancing work-life boundaries, and implementing security baselines learned through the GitHub Secure Open Source Fund.
items.bottom_line: Viral open source projects driven by AI tooling face unprecedented pull request floods that require automated filtering and robust contributor governance.

items.title: When to Use Encode-Prefill-Decode Disaggregation to Accelerate Multimodal Model Serving
items.summary: Encode-prefill-decode (EPD) disaggregation is an inference optimization technique for multimodal models that separates the vision encoder stage from the prefill and decode stages. It is most effective for image-heavy prompts, short-to-medium outputs, and quantized mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. items.title: Credentialed Pre-Port Discovery: Don't Probe the Host, Ask it
items.summary: If your scan engine already holds credentials for a host, it can ask that host which ports are open instead of probing for them. Every scan begins with the same question: which ports on this host are open? Everything after it, from identifying services to checking for vulnerabilities to evaluating policy, depends on the answer being right. The traditional answer comes from the outside: the scan engine sends traffic to a range of ports and infers each port's state from how the host responds. That approach is the industry standard, and it works well when a clear network path exists between the engine and the host.

items.title: Why is the x86 undefined instruction called ud2? Why 2?
items.summary: If you look at x86 compiler output (or if, like me, you’re looking at a crash caused by some software that tried to detour an API), you may see an instruction ud2. The ud2 instruction is an architecturally undefined instruction, guaranteed to raise an “invalid opcode” exception. Some compilers generate it to mark “unreachable” code, so that if execution somehow manages to reach it, you get a crash rather than executing random instructions. For example, if a function marked [[noreturn]] somehow returns, the compiler will put a ud2 after the call so that the program crashes instead of falling through to the next function. Anyway, why is this instruction called ud2 instead of just ud?
